explanation: Controlled reference test succeeded end-to-end. Environment: Python 3.13.13 (python:3.13.13-slim-bookworm) with pyhmmer==0.12.3 (the version declared by the source revision's pyproject.toml, installed from a prebuilt cp312-abi3 manylinux wheel, so no compiler was needed) plus its psutil dependency. The staging recipe fetched the notebook's two inputs (LuxC.sto Stockholm alignment, 8548 bytes; LuxC.faa protein FASTA, 12 sequences, 7302 bytes) from the pyhmmer repository at the reviewed revision and verified their sha256; the controller re-verified them byte-identical after the offline run (staged_inputs_verified: true, 2 files). The reference executed offline from a fresh working directory to exit 0 in 0.3s, printing the HMM consensus and the top domain alignment as in the notebook, and produced both declared artifacts: /work/outputs/LuxC.hmm (187150 bytes, HMMER3/f Plan7 model of 400 positions built from the LuxC alignment) and /work/outputs/LuxC.domtbl (4093 bytes, hmmsearch-style domain table with 11 reported domains over the 12 searched sequences, top hit tr|B6ESM7|B6ESM7_ALISL E-value 2e-169). Independent cross-check: executing the completely un-adapted conversion with the notebook's original relative data/msa and data/seqs layout yielded a byte-identical LuxC.domtbl (sha256 fc3da85a...) and an LuxC.hmm differing only in HMMER's build-time DATE and COM stamps, confirming the offline input-path adaptations preserved the exact bytes analyzed and changed no scientific result. The controller's semantic_fidelity_validated flag was false, which corresponds to the absence of an independent semantic validation step for this run (no error, mismatch or rejection was reported), and both artifacts matched the reviewed export plan.
source_adaptations: Input-path adaptation 1 of 2: in analysis.py the MSAFile path "data/msa/LuxC.sto" (relative to the notebook's working directory; docs/examples contains no data/msa directory, its .gitignore lists only generated outputs there) was changed to "/inputs/LuxC.sto", staged by stage-inputs.sh from https://raw.githubusercontent.com/althonos/pyhmmer/90d2f28303d9fe795c4e1ffc1e05b9d634319b51/src/pyhmmer/tests/data/msa/LuxC.sto (sha256 e2cf20e9c15473a9ee33634415327e64b2e77b482dd6e43f759123c22f2e0edc).

Input-path adaptation 2 of 2: in analysis.py the SequenceFile path "data/seqs/LuxC.faa" was changed to "/inputs/LuxC.faa", staged from https://raw.githubusercontent.com/althonos/pyhmmer/90d2f28303d9fe795c4e1ffc1e05b9d634319b51/src/pyhmmer/tests/data/seqs/LuxC.faa (sha256 7ce47aaed2c5e1eba1c683dc0be3efa11ee34038eb498cc09287c61c62b697d0). No other statement, parameter, import or scientific step was altered (verified: source diff contains only these two lines).

Fidelity evidence for both adaptations: running the unmodified conversion with the notebook's original relative input tree produced a byte-identical LuxC.domtbl (sha256 fc3da85a5d9a7c8bdb7ed7d3ff8d1114488e3707abf8f7311bd83a24186b563b) and an LuxC.hmm identical except for the DATE and COM header lines HMMER stamps with build time and command line at model construction, so the same input bytes were read and the same search results produced.
unresolved_assumptions: The notebook's relative input paths (data/msa/LuxC.sto, data/seqs/LuxC.faa) imply a data directory that is not present in the source tree at the reviewed revision; the files were located by repository tree search at src/pyhmmer/tests/data/{msa,seqs}. Their filenames, content (LuxC family alignment and LuxC protein sequences) and the successful reproduction of the notebook's expected results (12 sequences searched, significant hits for LuxC proteins) support this provenance, but this staging location is inferred rather than documented in the notebook itself; the sha256 values recorded in stage-inputs.sh pin the exact bytes.

pyhmmer 0.12.3 is the version chosen from evidence (the reviewed revision's own pyproject.toml declares version 0.12.3, matching the latest upstream release and the tested installation); the notebook itself records no version pin beyond pyhmmer.__version__, and floating-point outputs of a different pyhmmer/HMMER version could differ in detail.

The exported LuxC.hmm contains HMMER build-time metadata (DATE timestamp and COM command line) that necessarily varies between runs (observed different DATE/COM lines in two clean runs of the same code); the scientific content (model parameters, consensus, lengths) was observed stable across runs.

Hit counts and scores in LuxC.domtbl are execution-observed (11 reported domains, top E-value 2e-169) and confirmed stable across three independent runs with identical bytes, but were not checked against any upstream-recorded reference output.

The controller reported semantic_fidelity_validated: false alongside a successful run with no error; this was interpreted as no independent semantic validation being performed rather than a validation failure, since all declared files were produced and verified and no rejection message was returned.
